x: The mile which followed was won by Ingles of T.V.H. but Ray Tooby and Don McLean, both putting in a rare appearance, finished 2nd and 3rd. The quarter gave another opportunity for young Stephens to add to our score and this he ably did by securing 3rd place.
Jack was also in the invidious position of having two first class athletes in the persons of Mick Maynard, Herne Hill, and Ingles of T.V.H. ahead of him and not even in sight.

Barratt of Ealing was an easy winner in 43.17, followed by Olney 44.13, and Ingles another minute back, third Peter Bagnall ran well to be 4th in 45.42, but he had no backing from the rest who included Short 9th, Gebbett 12th, Abbott 13th, L.
Roffey and Bagnall gave of their best whilst Dave Baulch ran above form and forced himself past Ingles in the home straight to make sure we had six men home before T.V.H. had three.

West of Essex to bring us into 4th place but Maynard, H.H.H. and Ingles T.V.H. were closing the gap behind us. It should also be recorded that other notabilities on this stage were Sando, Driver, Heatley, O'Gorman, Keily and Ingles, all of whom beat the previous record and all of whom gained assistance in battling with the opposition.
